## blowhorn store

Report whether this computer can reach the Blowhorn database, and say why not when it cannot. With the default store (Blowhorn) that is the signed-in check. The Postgres store and its bastion tunnel are a maintainer tool (`BLOWHORN_MAINTAINER`=1). One bounded probe: the bastion tunnel is up (and is opened if it is not), the server answers, the schema matches the migrations this checkout ships, the configured organization resolves, and the local write-back spool is empty.

The connection is Blowhorn's own configuration -- host, port, database, user, password and the tunnel, under `store.` in ~/.config/blowhorn/store.yaml (mode 0600), settable with `blowhorn config set` and in the desktop app. `--replay-spool` drains results already waiting in the spool, against Blowhorn on the default store and against Postgres for a maintainer. Apart from it and `--import`, nothing here writes anything.

Exits 0 when the store is usable, 2 when two flags contradict each other and 3 when the store is not usable -- the same code every other command uses for an unreachable store, so a wrapper can tell an outage from a failed job. `--json` emits the probe as one object: configured, configPath, configMode, dsn (password elided), tunnel \{enabled, up, error\}, reachable, serverVersion, schema \{applied, pending\}, organization, spoolDepth, validation, error, plus ok, exitCode, cause, warnings, rungs, offline, properties and replay.

```text
blowhorn store [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit the probe as machine-readable JSON (the shape the desktop app's Setup row reads); the password is elided in the reported dsn on every surface |
| `--offline` | boolean | `false` | Answer from the configured paths and the files on disk alone: no tunnel is opened and no connection is attempted. This is how you tell a wrong setting from a dropped tunnel without waiting for three connect attempts to time out. It cannot be combined with `--replay-spool`, which needs the connection it refuses to open |
| `--import` | string |  | Maintainer only (`BLOWHORN_MAINTAINER`=1). Prints every property it set, with the password reported as set rather than echoed. With `--dry-run` the report is printed and nothing is written. It cannot be combined with `--replay-spool`: run `blowhorn store --replay-spool` after the import |
| `--replay-spool` | boolean | `false` | Write out the results waiting in the local write-back spool now, rather than leaving them for the next run to drain. On the default Blowhorn store that drain runs against Blowhorn and reports how many write-backs were pushed, kept and dropped. An entry whose activity no longer exists is named and dropped from the pending file (the month's ledger still holds it); nothing else is ever deleted. With `--dry-run` it writes nothing and reports what the run without it would have done. It is refused with `--offline` or `--import`, because a replay needs a connection those do not open |
| `--platform` | string |  | Accepted and ignored by `blowhorn store`: this command never acts on a platform, so `--platform` has no effect here -- including a value inherited from `BLOWHORN_PLATFORM` or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by `blowhorn store` because `--pace` is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then `BLOWHORN_PACE`, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn store --import
blowhorn store
blowhorn store --json
blowhorn store --offline
blowhorn store --replay-spool
blowhorn store --replay-spool --dry-run
```

Output: json with `--json`, text otherwise.
